verdict.rationale: Sentry has an official MCP server that connects external AI assistants for searching errors and analyzing performance. It also has a documented web API, with a published OpenAPI 3.0.3 schema covering /api/0/, for programmatic access and data export, so an external agent can query error and performance/trace data. The evidence does not show that logs or metrics can be queried through these APIs; logs appear only as OTLP ingestion, and the v0 API includes beta endpoints. missing for 10: documented agent/API querying of logs, documented metrics query API, independent hands-on corroboration of agent-driven production debugging.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an external agent query metrics, logs, and traces through documented APIs to debug production

citations.quote: Connects AI assistants to Sentry for searching errors, analyzing performance, triaging issues, reading documentation, and managing projects — all via the Model Context Protocol.
The Sentry web API is used to access the Sentry platform programmatically. You can use the APIs to manage account-level resources, like organizations and teams, as well as manage and export data.
The official getsentry/sentry-api-schema repository publishes the dereferenced OpenAPI 3.0.3 document for the "Sentry Public API"
